TIEC 03-03:

      Please provide any summaries EPE possesses of the BAAJA.


RESPONSE:

      The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) of 2026 was introduced as

      proposed legislation in September 2026. The following analysis addresses its proposed

      requirements, not existing binding law.


      The BAAJA could have implications for large-load tariffs designed to serve data centers

      and AI computing facilities.

      An important provision is Section 2107, Ratepayer Protection, which would establish

      federal cost-causation requirements for data centers while preserving substantial state

      regulatory authority over retail rates.

TIEC 03-06:

      What is EPE’s understanding as to whether, if it became law, the BAAJA ratepayer

      protection provisions on data centers and other computational loads would be mandatory

      on EPE? Would the BAAJA, if it became law, require changes to EPE’s proposed tariff in

      this case?



RESPONSE:

      EPE expects that the federal law, if enacted, will apply to EPE. EPE has not evaluated

      whether the current version of the bill would require changes to the proposed Schedule 27,

      but the legislation in its current form preserves substantial state regulatory authority over

      retail rates.
